title: Star Fox
designer: Jez San, Dylan Cuthbert, Giles Goddard
shortDescription: Nintendo and Argonaut's revolutionary 3D polygon shooter on SNES, powered by the ground-breaking Super FX coprocessor chip.
historicalSignificance: Pioneered real-time 3D polygonal gaming on home consoles via the revolutionary Super FX coprocessor, moving over 4 million copies and launching the iconic Fox McCloud franchise.

editorialContent.overview: Partnering with British technology studio Argonaut Games, Nintendo integrated a custom RISC coprocessor (the Super FX) directly inside the cartridge to render real-time textured 3D polygons on the 16-bit SNES.
editorialContent.gameplay: Players pilot the Arwing starfighter through the Lylat System to defeat the evil scientist Andross, performing barrel rolls, utilizing smart bombs, and maneuvering through multiple branching difficulty routes.
editorialContent.technicalInnovation: The Super FX chip acted as a math coprocessor, calculating 3D polygon math and rendering shaded polyhedral models directly into the SNES frame buffer at over 15–20 FPS.
editorialContent.culturalImpact: Proved that true 3D gaming was viable on consumer home consoles, setting the stage for the fifth-generation 3D revolution.
editorialContent.preservationNotes: Preserved on original Super FX cartridges and included on the Super NES Classic Edition.

awards: Electronic Gaming Monthly Best Shooter of 1993
